title: Aesop's Fables
author: Aesop
description: Three hundred very short animal stories, each ending in a moral: the tortoise and the hare, the boy who cried wolf, the fox and the grapes. Perfect bite-sized reading.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
description: Alice falls down a rabbit hole into a world of talking animals, riddles and nonsense — a playful tour of real, vivid English.

title: Anne of Green Gables
author: L. M. Montgomery
description: An imaginative orphan girl with red hair and a big vocabulary transforms a quiet farm in Prince Edward Island. Charming and full of vivid speech.

title: Around the World in Eighty Days
author: Jules Verne
description: Phileas Fogg bets he can circle the globe in eighty days and races against the clock with his loyal servant Passepartout. A fast, fun plot in clear prose.

title: Black Beauty
author: Anna Sewell
description: A gentle horse tells the story of his life with many different owners. Short chapters, simple sentences and a strong message about kindness.

title: The Call of the Wild
author: Jack London
description: A strong pet dog is stolen and sold as a sled dog in the frozen Yukon. He must grow wild to survive — a gripping tale of instinct and endurance.

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
description: On Christmas Eve, the miser Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by three spirits who show him his past, present and future. A short, unforgettable classic.

title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court
author: Mark Twain
description: A modern American engineer is knocked on the head and wakes up in Camelot, where he tries to bring 19th-century technology to King Arthur's court. Hilarious and sharp.

title: David Copperfield
author: Charles Dickens
description: From a lonely childhood to fame as a writer, David Copperfield is Dickens's most personal novel — full of unforgettable characters like Mr. Micawber and Uriah Heep.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
description: A beautiful young man stays forever young while a hidden portrait ages in his place. Wilde's only novel is full of sharp epigrams about beauty and vice.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description: The vampire Count Dracula comes to England, and a small group must hunt him down. Told through letters and diaries — suspenseful and deeply atmospheric.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
description: Emma is sure she is an excellent matchmaker — until her plans backfire in delightful ways. Witty, warm and full of Austen's sharpest social comedy.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description: A scientist creates a living creature and then abandons it, with tragic results. Written when the author was eighteen, it asks what it means to be human.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
description: An orphan boy called Pip is suddenly raised from his humble life by a mysterious fortune. A sweeping story of money, class and self-discovery.

title: Grimms' Fairy Tales
author: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm
description: Two hundred tales of kings, dwarfs, wolves and magic — from Rapunzel and Cinderella to Hansel and Gretel. The classic source of the stories everyone knows.

title: Gulliver's Travels
author: Jonathan Swift
description: Shipwrecked Gulliver visits lands of tiny people, giant people and talking horses. A famous adventure that is secretly a sharp satire on human nature.

title: Hard Times
author: Charles Dickens
description: In the bleak industrial city of Coketown, a schoolmaster who believes only in facts learns what really matters. Short, fierce and deeply funny.

title: Heidi
author: Johanna Spyri
description: A sunny-natured orphan girl is sent to live with her gruff grandfather high in the Swiss Alps. Simple, joyful prose perfect for early learners.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: A ghostly hound haunts the moors around Baskerville Hall, and Holmes must uncover the truth behind a family curse. The most famous of the Sherlock Holmes novels.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
author: Mark Twain
description: Huck Finn escapes his violent father and floats down the Mississippi on a raft with Jim, an escaped slave. Funny and moving, with unforgettable American voices.

title: The Invisible Man
author: H. G. Wells
description: A scientist discovers how to make himself invisible — and uses his power to terrify a quiet English village. Suspenseful, funny and unsettling.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: An orphan girl grows up poor, becomes a governess, and falls in love with her mysterious employer. A first-person story rich in feeling and atmosphere.

title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: A respected doctor invents a potion that lets him become his evil double. A short, terrifying study of the good and evil inside every person.

title: A Journey to the Centre of the Earth
author: Jules Verne
description: A professor decodes a cryptic message and descends into a volcano with his nephew, into a lost world of prehistoric marvels. Verne at his most adventurous.

title: The Jungle Book
author: Rudyard Kipling
description: Mowgli is raised by wolves in the Indian jungle, learning the Law of the Jungle from Baloo the bear and Bagheera the panther. Seven classic stories.

title: Just So Stories
author: Rudyard Kipling
description: Twelve funny origin stories: how the leopard got his spots, the camel his hump, and the elephant his trunk. Playful, rhythmic English that begs to be read aloud.

title: Les Misérables
author: Victor Hugo
description: Jean Valjean steals a loaf of bread and spends his life running from the law, seeking redemption in a world of poverty and revolution. One of the greatest novels ever written.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
description: The four March sisters grow up in Civil War America, dreaming, quarrelling and loving each other. A warm story about family and becoming yourself.

title: Mansfield Park
author: Jane Austen
description: Quiet Fanny Price is taken in by her wealthy relatives at Mansfield Park and must find her place among them. Austen's deepest study of character and conscience.

title: The Memoirs of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Eleven short adventures including Silver Blaze, The Musgrave Ritual and the final confrontation at Reichenbach Falls. Holmes at his sharpest.

title: The Metamorphosis
author: Franz Kafka
description: Gregor Samsa wakes up one morning as a giant insect. Surreal, dark and strangely funny — the most famous short story of the twentieth century.

title: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale
author: Herman Melville
description: Ishmael signs onto a whaling ship and meets the obsessed Captain Ahab, who hunts one great white whale. Huge, strange and magnificent — the great American novel.

title: Northanger Abbey
author: Jane Austen
description: A young woman who reads too many Gothic novels visits a mysterious abbey and lets her imagination run wild. A sparkling parody and a sweet romance.

title: Oliver Twist
author: Charles Dickens
description: A poor orphan asks for more porridge and is thrown into a world of thieves and villains. Dickens's most famous attack on cruelty — and a great adventure.

title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
description: Dorothy is swept away to a magical land and must travel the yellow brick road. Warm, clear prose that learners can really sink into.

title: Persuasion
author: Jane Austen
description: Years after Anne Elliot was persuaded to refuse the man she loved, he returns — rich and still unmarried. Austen's most tender and mature novel.

title: Peter Pan
author: J. M. Barrie
description: The boy who never grows up takes Wendy and her brothers to Neverland, where they fight pirates and fly with fairies. Playful, quotable English.

title: The Adventures of Pinocchio
author: Carlo Collodi
description: A wooden puppet who wants to be a real boy keeps getting into trouble. Clear, lively storytelling that is ideal for early readers.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: Elizabeth Bennet meets the proud Mr. Darcy and both must learn to see past first impressions. Sharp, witty dialogue and one of the best-loved novels in English.

title: The Prince and the Pauper
author: Mark Twain
description: A poor boy and a prince who look exactly alike swap clothes — and lives. A fast, funny story about justice, kindness and seeing the world through another's eyes.

title: The Return of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Holmes returns from the dead in thirteen brilliant short cases, from The Empty House to The Second Stain. Vintage detective work at its peak.

title: Robinson Crusoe
author: Daniel Defoe
description: A sailor shipwrecked alone on a tropical island must build a life from almost nothing. The original survival story, told with plain, practical detail.

title: The Scarlet Letter
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: In Puritan New England, Hester Prynne must wear a scarlet letter for the rest of her life. A powerful novel about guilt, secrecy and courage.

title: The Secret Garden
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
description: A lonely girl discovers a hidden, walled garden and, as it blooms, so does she. A warm story about nature, friendship and growing up.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Twelve classic short stories about the world's greatest detective and his friend Dr. Watson, from A Scandal in Bohemia to The Copper Beeches.

title: A Study in Scarlet
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: The very first Sherlock Holmes story: a mysterious murder in an empty house and the meeting of Holmes and Dr. Watson. Where the legend began.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
description: A doctor, a lawyer and a wine-shop keeper are caught up in the French Revolution. Epic, suspenseful and home to the most famous ending in English fiction.

title: The Three Musketeers
author: Alexandre Dumas
description: Young d'Artagnan joins Athos, Porthos and Aramis — the king's musketeers — for duels, conspiracies and the famous diamond affair. The great adventure novel.

title: Through the Looking-Glass
author: Lewis Carroll
description: Alice steps through the mirror into a backward world of chess pieces, nonsense poems and the Jabberwock. The playful sequel to Wonderland.

title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
description: An inventor travels to the year 802701 and finds humanity split into two strange races. Short, vivid and thought-provoking — an early classic of science fiction.

title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
author: Mark Twain
description: Tom Sawyer tricks his friends, plays truant, and hunts for treasure on the Mississippi. Funny, warm and packed with everyday American English.

title: Treasure Island
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: Young Jim Hawkins finds a treasure map and sails to a distant island full of pirates, including the famous Long John Silver. Action-packed and easy to follow.

title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas
author: Jules Verne
description: A mysterious sea monster turns out to be the submarine Nautilus, commanded by the enigmatic Captain Nemo. A grand voyage full of marine marvels.

title: Vanity Fair
author: William Makepeace Thackeray
description: Becky Sharp climbs the slippery ladder of English society with wit and no conscience. A huge, satirical novel about ambition, money and pretending.

title: The War of the Worlds
author: H. G. Wells
description: Martians invade Victorian England with terrible war machines. Tense, suspenseful prose with striking descriptions and a famous twist at the end.

title: White Fang
author: Jack London
description: The story of a wild wolf-dog in the frozen North who must learn to trust humans. The fierce companion to The Call of the Wild.

title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
description: Mole, Rat, Badger and Mr. Toad by the river — gentle adventures full of friendship and lovely descriptions of the English countryside.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
description: On the wild Yorkshire moors, the fierce love between Heathcliff and Catherine shapes two families for generations. Dark, stormy and unforgettable.

title: The Yellow Wallpaper
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
description: A woman is told to rest and never to think, and slowly the pattern of the yellow wallpaper starts to move. A chilling short story in the form of a diary.
